# Creating search stores

## Prerequisites

- The Data and Search Platform is deployed: `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}`
- You can reach it with one of: `curl`, the Sherlock Python SDK (`sherlock-client`), or the platform CLI ([`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli)).
- You understand the search store concept — see [Core concepts](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/core-concepts.html).

| | About the `sherlock` hostname `sherlock` is the internal name of the platform’s retrieval service, the component that serves the HTTP API (search stores, uploads, search). For this reason, the API URL is `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}`. A deployment also includes an ingestion worker pool that executes workflows in the background. You do not call the worker pool directly. The full component list is in [Resource requirements](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/resource-requirements.html#components). |
|---|---|

## Client setup

Each example below is shown for three clients. All three call the same REST API at `https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}/api/v1`; the SDK and the CLI wrap the requests shown in the **curl** tab. Every request requires a bearer token. The deployment’s IAM sidecar validates the token and adds the caller’s user identity to the request, and Sherlock authorizes the request against that identity.

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

Log in once with the platform CLI, then export the deployment URL and a token:

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser

export SHERLOCK_URL="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}"
export AA_TOKEN="$(pharia --env aleph-alpha iam token)"
```

Pass `-H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"` on every call. A platform token from any other source also works; the API only reads the header. Requests with a JSON body use `--json` (curl 7.82.0 or later), which sends the body and sets the `Content-Type` and `Accept` headers to `application/json`. To read the body from a file, use `--json @body.json`.

Install the client from the Aleph Alpha package index:

```bash
pip install sherlock-client --extra-index-url https://alephalpha.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/pypi/holmes/simple
```

Then create a client for the deployment:

```python
import os

from sherlock import SyncSherlock

client = SyncSherlock(
    url="https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}",
    token=os.environ["AA_TOKEN"],
)
```

`url` and `token` default to the `SHERLOCK_BASE_URL` and `SHERLOCK_TOKEN` environment variables, so `SyncSherlock()` without arguments works when those variables are set. `Sherlock` is the async client and has the same API. Use either client as a context manager (`with SyncSherlock(...) as client:`) to close the connection pool when you finish.

The platform CLI ([`pharia`](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/pharia-cli)) handles authentication. Log in once; every subsequent command uses the cached token:

```bash
pharia iam login    # one-time OAuth login via your browser
```

Select the environment with the global `--env` flag, for example `pharia --env aleph-alpha iam login`. The CLI caches tokens per environment and refreshes them automatically. To reach a deployment that the CLI does not know, pass `--base-url https://sherlock.{ingressDomain}` or set `PHARIA_SHERLOCK_URL`. To use the token in your own tooling, print it with `TOKEN=$(pharia iam token)`.

![Overview of the pharia iam commands](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/COMMON/_images/pharia-data-cli-iam.png)

## 1. Choose your embedding configuration

Each entry in a store’s `models` array describes one vector space. The following table lists all accepted values:

| Field | Accepted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `embedding_model` | any model identifier your deployment exposes | Free-form string, normalised to lowercase (`BAAI/bge-m3` and `baai/bge-m3` are the same model). It does not affect which collection the store uses. It only determines which vectors inside the collection are matched. |
| `type` | `dense`, `bm25` | `dense` for semantic similarity; `bm25` for exact lexical matching. Use one of each for [hybrid search](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/searching.html#hybrid-search-dense-bm25). A `bm25` entry must be `modality: "text"` with `distance: "dot"` and no `dimension`/`embedding_model` (the lexical vector is computed in-process). At most one `bm25` entry per store. `sparse`, `multi`, and `quantized` are reserved and rejected at creation. |
| `distance` | `cosine`, `dot`, `euclid`, `manhattan` | `cosine` for text embeddings in almost all cases. Note the spelling `euclid`, not `euclidean`. Anything outside this set is rejected with `400`. |
| `modality` | `text`, `image`, `audio`, `cross-modal` | `text` for document search; the rest depend on which embedding models your deployment exposes. |
| `dimension` | positive integer, or omitted | The embedding model’s output size. Omit it only for variable-width vectors such as `bm25`. A dense entry without a positive `dimension` is rejected with `400`. |
| `qdrant` | per-vector index tuning | Optional low-level override: `on_disk`, `hnsw_config`, `quantization_config`, `datatype`, `multivector_config`. Leave it unset unless the collection requires specific tuning. |

Any combination of these enum values passes validation. A typo in `type`, `distance`, or `modality` is rejected as an invalid value; it is not silently mapped to another value.

All stores with the same combination of `type`, `modality`, `distance`, and `dimension` share one vector-database collection. That collection must exist before you can create the store; see [how search stores are stored](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/core-concepts.html#advanced-how-search-stores-are-stored). `GET /api/v1/collections` lists the provisioned collections. If you choose a configuration that is not provisioned, the API returns `422 Collection Not Provisioned` (see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/troubleshooting.html)). A platform admin can provision it on request.

## 2. Create a search store

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "name": "my-store",
    "models": [
      {
        "embedding_model": "your-embedding-model",
        "type": "dense",
        "dimension": 1024,
        "distance": "cosine",
        "modality": "text"
      }
    ],
    "fusion_strategy": {"type": "rrf", "params": {"k": 60}},
    "access_policy": "private"
  }'
```

```python
store = client.v1.search_stores.create(
    name="my-store",
    models=[
        {
            "embedding_model": "your-embedding-model",
            "type": "dense",
            "dimension": 1024,
            "distance": "cosine",
            "modality": "text",
        }
    ],
    fusion_strategy={"type": "rrf", "params": {"k": 60}},
    access_policy="private",
)

print(store.id)
```

`create` returns a store handle. `store.id` is the ID you use in later calls. `store.files`, `store.workflows`, and `store.documents` are the store-scoped namespaces for ingestion and retrieval.

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock stores create \
  --name my-store \
  --models '[{
    "embedding_model": "your-embedding-model",
    "type": "dense",
    "dimension": 1024,
    "distance": "cosine",
    "modality": "text"
  }]' \
  --fusion-strategy '{"type": "rrf", "params": {"k": 60}}' \
  --access-policy private
```

JSON flag values also accept `@file` or `@-` for stdin.

The response includes the store’s `id`. Use it in every subsequent request. `access_policy` defaults to `private`: only you can see or use the store.

For hybrid search, add a second `models` entry with `"type": "bm25"`, `"modality": "text"`, `"distance": "dot"`, and no other fields. `fusion_strategy` controls how the dense and lexical results are combined: `rrf`, `convex`, `anchored`, `dbsf`, or `dense_only`. If you omit it for a dense + bm25 pair, the default is `convex` when the dense entry uses `cosine` or `dot`, and `rrf` otherwise. A non-empty `weights` is rejected.

| | Version availability Hybrid `bm25` stores are available from Data and Search Platform release 0.9.0, bundled in PhariaAI 1.260900.0. Older deployments accept a `"type": "sparse"` entry at creation, but no ingestion workflow populates it, so searches on those stores use only the dense vectors. |
|---|---|

`models` cannot be changed after creation. Search filters on the declared model, so a change would make every vector already written unreachable. To use a different configuration, create a new store.

### Declaring filterable metadata

Ingestion can attach arbitrary metadata to chunks. The platform stores all of it under the `metadata.` prefix in the vector payload. Metadata attached at [file upload](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/ingesting-files.html#attach-metadata-to-uploads) is stored under the `user` sub-namespace, so declare those fields with the `user.` prefix (`"path": "user.site"`). To filter on a metadata field, declare it as an index when you create the store:

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "name": "my-store",
    "models": [
      {
        "embedding_model": "your-embedding-model",
        "type": "dense",
        "dimension": 1024,
        "distance": "cosine",
        "modality": "text"
      }
    ],
    "metadata_indexes": [
      {"path": "language",     "type": "string"},
      {"path": "year",         "type": "integer"},
      {"path": "draft",        "type": "boolean"},
      {"path": "published_at", "type": "datetime"}
    ]
  }'
```

```python
store = client.v1.search_stores.create(
    name="my-store",
    models=[
        {
            "embedding_model": "your-embedding-model",
            "type": "dense",
            "dimension": 1024,
            "distance": "cosine",
            "modality": "text",
        }
    ],
    metadata_indexes=[
        {"path": "language", "type": "string"},
        {"path": "year", "type": "integer"},
        {"path": "draft", "type": "boolean"},
        {"path": "published_at", "type": "datetime"},
    ],
)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock stores create \
  --name my-store \
  --models @models.json \
  --metadata-indexes '[
    {"path": "language", "type": "string"},
    {"path": "year",     "type": "integer"},
    {"path": "draft",    "type": "boolean"},
    {"path": "published_at", "type": "datetime"}
  ]'
```

Each entry has a `path` and a `type`. The `path` is the metadata key; the platform resolves it to `metadata.<path>` for indexing and filtering. The `type` selects the index kind in the vector database, so it must match the type of the values your ingestion writes. The following table lists all supported types:

| `type` | Index created | Filter it with | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `string` | keyword | `match.value`, `match.any` | Use for IDs, language codes, tags, and enum-like values. If declared with `"prefix": true`, the index also supports `match.prefix`. |
| `integer` | integer | `match.value`, `match.any`, `range` | |
| `float` | float | `range` | Use range bounds, not `match.value`. A fractional value in `match.value` matches nothing, and a whole-number value (`2.0`) is matched as an integer. |
| `boolean` | bool | `match.value` with `true`/`false` | |
| `datetime` | datetime | `range` with RFC 3339 bounds | Write the values as RFC 3339 timestamps (`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and filter with the same, for example `{"field": "metadata.published_at", "range": {"gte": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}}`. Mixing timestamp and numeric bounds in one range returns `400`. |

Any other `type` is rejected as an unsupported metadata index type. A blank `path` is also rejected.

| | Version availability `"prefix": true` and the `match.prefix` operator are available from release 0.9.0. |
|---|---|

Before you choose your fields, note the following constraints:

- **You must declare a field to filter on it.** A search whose filter references an undeclared `metadata.<path>` is rejected with `400`, and the error names the field: *"field is not filterable on this search store; declare it in metadata_indexes"*. The vector database does not filter on unindexed fields, so the store validates the filter before sending it and returns a specific error. Declare every metadata field you intend to filter on.
- **System fields are always filterable**: `file_id`, `document_id`, `page_id`, `chunk_id`, `workflow_id`, `workflow_run_id`. Do not declare them.
- **You can declare indexes only at creation.** The API does not support updating them, because rebuilding an index over an existing collection can be expensive. To add a field later, create a new store. Declarations are additive, and a path’s type cannot change once set. Because [collections are shared by geometry](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/core-concepts.html#advanced-how-search-stores-are-stored), the indexes on the underlying collection are the union of the declarations of all stores that share it. Each store still accepts filters only on its own declared fields: an index declared by another store on the same collection does not make the field filterable in yours.

## 3. Share a search store (optional)

To make a store readable by any authenticated user, update its `access_policy`:

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl -X PUT "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{"access_policy": "public"}'
```

```python
client.v1.search_stores("<store-id>").update(access_policy="public")
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock stores update <store-id> --access-policy public
```

To share with specific users or groups, grant them **viewer** or **writer** access:

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl -X PUT "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores/<store-id>/permissions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN" \
  --json '{
    "add": {
      "viewers": ["user:<user-id>"],
      "writers": ["group:<group-id>"]
    }
  }'
```

The response contains the store’s full sharing state after the change: `access_policy`, `owner_id`, `viewers`, and `writers`. To revoke access, send a `"remove"` object with the same shape. Removes are applied before adds, so a subject listed in both is granted access.

```python
state = client.v1.search_stores("<store-id>").update_permissions(
    add={
        "viewers": ["user:<user-id>"],
        "writers": ["group:<group-id>"],
    },
)

print(state.viewers, state.writers)
```

To revoke access, pass `remove=` with the same shape. Both arguments are keyword-only.

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock stores permissions <store-id> \
  --add-viewer user:<user-id> \
  --add-writer group:<group-id>
```

Only the store’s owner can change `access_policy`, delete the store, or manage its permissions. Any authenticated user can read a public store, and it appears in their store list; see [Multi-user isolation and sharing](https://docs.aleph-alpha.com/phariaai-dev-guide/latest/pharia-data/core-concepts.html#multi-user-isolation-and-sharing). To stop public sharing, set the policy back to `private`. To revoke individual grants, send the same subjects under `remove` instead of `add` (`--remove-viewer`/`--remove-writer` on the CLI).

## Validation

- curl
- Python SDK
- Platform CLI

```bash
curl "$SHERLOCK_URL/api/v1/search-stores" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AA_TOKEN"
```

```python
page = client.v1.search_stores.list(limit=20, offset=0)

for store in page:
    print(store.id, store.name, store.access_policy)
print(page.total)
```

```bash
pharia --env aleph-alpha sherlock stores list
```

This lists the stores you own and all public stores. Confirm that your new store appears with the expected `id`.

## Troubleshooting

### Collection not provisioned

- **Error**: `422 Collection Not Provisioned`
- **Solution**: The embedding configuration in `models` maps to a collection that is not provisioned. Ask a platform admin to provision it, or choose a configuration that is already available.

### Authorisation errors

- **Error**: 401 Unauthorized
- **Solution**: Check that your token has not expired and is correctly formatted.
- **Error**: 403 Forbidden
- **Solution**: You are authenticated but lack the required permission on this store, for example when you change `access_policy` without being the owner.
